title: Docker Compose
interviewAnswer: Compose defines a multi-container application—such as API, database, Kafka, Redis and workers—in one declarative file. Multiple containers may reuse the same image with different commands.
why: Docker Compose is a simple way to define and run multi-container applications locally or in small environments.
intuition: One YAML file describes services, images/builds, environment variables, networks, volumes and dependencies so the whole stack starts consistently.
deepDive: Each service usually runs one container role, but multiple services can share the same image with different commands. Compose creates a default network and DNS by service name. Volumes persist data. depends_on controls startup ordering but does not automatically guarantee application readiness unless health checks/conditions are used appropriately.
workedExample: A real-time telemetry platform can run Kafka, Redis, Flink JobManager/TaskManager, a producer, backend API and frontend as separate services; JobManager and TaskManager can still use the same Flink image with different commands.
code:
services:
  api:
    build: ./backend
    ports: ["8000:8000"]
  redis:
    image: redis:7
commonMistakes: Assuming one container always requires one unique image.
Using depends_on as a readiness check.
Persisting state only inside a container writable layer.
production: Compose is excellent for local integration/testing; large production systems usually need an orchestrator/platform for health, scaling and rollout.
